transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I’m here because I can’t seem to stop noticing this spot on my face. It’s like this rough, kind of sunken-looking patch, especially in photos or when I catch myself in the mirror. One side of my face just looks old and beat-up to me.

People tell me they barely see anything, which almost makes me feel crazier, you know? Like when you’ve been working outside for years, concrete dust and sun and all that, you start noticing every little thing. But this… I keep seeing it, and it’s been hard to just let it go.
How much is this concern about the spot on your face affecting your daily life or causing you distress?

It’s… yeah, it’s getting in the way more than I want to admit. Like in the mornings, I’ll be ready for a construction job and then I catch my face in the mirror, and suddenly I’m messing around trying to see if it looks as bad in different light. Then I’m late getting out the door.

And, uh… there’s stuff I avoid now. If the guys are taking site photos, I kind of step away or make sure I’m not in them. My family does game nights sometimes, and I’ve skipped a few because I just don’t want everybody looking at my face the whole time. I know they’re probably not, but it feels that way.
Do you feel anxious or really unsettled if you can't check your face in the mirror or if you can't avoid showing it off, like when you're at work or with family?

Yeah… I do. Like before work, I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror, turning my face this way and that under the light, trying to see if that patch is showing bad. I’ll rub at it too, which I know probably doesn’t help.

Same thing if I’m supposed to go to my sister’s game night. I’ll check it a bunch, and then I start thinking, well, maybe if I wear my hat low it won’t be so obvious. Or I’ll just make some excuse not to go. I mean, I’ve always worn hats on job sites anyway, you know, sun and dust and all that… but now it’s more like hiding. It gets me pretty unsettled if I can’t do something about it.
